relevance_note: Japanese family case report of two brothers with LCAT deficiency diagnosed biochemically: "revealing two homozygotes with a markedly low HDL"; no LCAT variant is printed (1989, no genotyping).
method_note: Read by hand; a Python script only assembled the JSON and checked spans. No LCAT variant is printed anywhere: the two brothers (Case 1/III-18, Case 2/III-21) are called homozygotes from LCAT mass/activity and family data, not sequencing (also once 'are suspected as homozygotes'); their variant rows have variant_original_string 'not reported' and zygosity 'homozygous' as the authors state it. Relatives are in scope as described relatives tested biochemically (LCAT mass/activity); only those the text names individually were extracted (II-3, III-3, III-4, III-9, III-12, III-14, III-8, II-11, II-15, IV-1, IV-2), plus the proband's father (deceased; authors infer he 'must have been a homozygote', not tested) and mother (LCAT mass 4.8). Table 3 (23 members) is badly garbled by OCR (header and generation labels lost, columns misaligned); it was not used, so about ten further family members appearing only in Table 3 got no rows, and relatives' ages/sex from Table 3 were not taken. Tables 1 and 2 (lab values for Case 1 and Case 2) are partly garbled; values were taken from the text where possible. Possible duplicate: the mother (LCAT mass 4.8) may be the same person as II-11 (maternal kindred with normal mass; Table 3 row 'l l' shows 4.8) but the paper never says so; kept separate, not merged. The 'no symptoms of LCAT deficiency' group statement (remaining 21 members) was recorded as an excluded feature for named relatives and the mother, but not used to exclude specific checklist items. Case 2's corneal opacity, low apo A-I, rouleaux and target cells come from 'Our two patients were homozygotes and had all these characteristic features' (inferred from group statement). General normal findings for Case 1 ('No abnormalities were detected in the peripheral blood cells, urine, liver or renal function tests') were recorded as written and exclude no specific checklist item; the paper qualifies the blood-cell statement with target-cell poikilocytosis in the next sentence. Internal inconsistencies: Case 1 ester cholesterol ratio '13%' vs '30%of total serum cholesterol', and HDL-C '9 mg/dl' vs '18 mg/dl' (different occasions); maternal kindred activity '58' in Discussion vs '5 9' in Table 3; mother's mass given in 'µg/dl' vs µg/ml elsewhere. Abstract per-patient values ('0.8 and 0.9 μg/ml, respectively') were not assigned by position. Publication year not printed (only 'Received for publication May 27, 1989'), so year is null.
